target_customer: Individuals, creators and small businesses making vertical social video for Instagram, TikTok and similar feeds, via a freemium subscription
problem: Making polished animated Stories and Reels normally needs design skill and desktop tools. Mojo gives templates and animated text so non-designers can produce pro-looking vertical video on a phone.
business_model: Freemium consumer subscription (Pro plan, about 39.99 dollars a year in later reviews; 19.99 pounds a year in a 2019 review)

founders.name: Francescu Santoni
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and gives no background. One search snippet said Jean Patry is also listed on YC, but the page I opened did not show him, so he is not recorded.

exit.acquirer: Dailymotion (acquired Archery, the company behind Mojo)

technical_complexity.rationale: A template and animation engine for a phone, which is standard mobile engineering with some rendering work. No research-grade problem was reported.

defensibility.rationale: Templates and animated text were copyable by InShot, Adobe and later CapCut. No data or network moat was reported.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Adobe Spark and later Canva and CapCut offered overlapping features. Mojo survived as an independent app until Dailymotion bought its parent in 2025.

market_need_then: Instagram Stories launched in 2016 and brands and creators wanted animated vertical content without design skills. A 2019 review shows the app at 19 templates and a paid tier. No 2018 spend data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses mojo-app.com, so not the exact mojo.com.

identity.visual_style: Orange brand color (hex F97632 per a brand listing)

rebrands.to: Mojo: Reels and Video Captions / AI Video and Reels Editor
rebrands.why: App Store titles changed over time as the product shifted from Stories to Reels and captions; no reason was stated by a source

brand_strength.rationale: Reviewed in a few niche outlets such as Journalism UK and Blog du Moderateur, but the name is shared with many other companies and no brand-driven growth was found.

outcome_analysis: Mojo stayed a small Paris team with a freemium Stories template app and later pivoted toward Reels and AI captions. It reached large download counts (one search source claimed more than 50 million) and was bought through its parent Archery by Dailymotion in 2025, with no disclosed price and no public funding record. It is a modest exit rather than a failure, but the funding and price are unknown.
notes: Funding: no round with a stated amount was found. A directory listed a YC seed on 2018-03-22 with unknown amount (unverified, not a round). The company site returned little detail. Sources disagree on closing month (May 2025 per CB Insights, June 2025 per Dailymotion); the Dailymotion release is used. The 50 million downloads figure comes from a secondary outlet. No dated 2018 competitor source was found, so the list is empty.
